```{r load}
library(wet)
library(ggplot2)
sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)

vd <- function(f) system.file("vignette-data", f, package = "wet")
v <- readRDS(vd("segment_values.rds"))
prov <- v$provenance
pub <- prov$published
map <- readRDS(vd("segment_map.rds"))
bc <- readRDS(vd("station_map.rds"))$bc

# the segment values below are the published product's, each checked against
# what it was built from by data-raw/segment_vignette_data.R: none may differ
stopifnot(identical(pub$manifest, wet:::wet_catalog_url), all(prov$published_check$compared > 0),
          all(prov$published_check$differing == 0))

# colours come from the gq registries, so no hex literal appears in this
# vignette; assert each class set, because a malformed CSV row adds a layer silently
reg <- gq::gq_reg_custom(system.file("cartography", "wet_segment.csv", package = "wet"))
reg_main <- gq::gq_reg_main()
classes <- function(layer, expect) {
  x <- gq::gq_tmap_classes(reg$layers[[layer]])
  stopifnot(identical(names(x$values), expect))
  list(values = x$values, labels = stats::setNames(x$labels, names(x$values)))
}
pal_mad <- classes("mad_class", paste0("m", 1:6))
pal_map <- classes("segment_map", c("group", "outline"))
pal_skill <- classes("skill_nesting", c("headwater", "nested"))
pal_guide <- classes("guide", "one_to_one")
pal_err <- classes("gauge_error", paste0("e", 1:4))
pal_prov <- classes("province", c("coverage", "zone", "group"))
pal_ctx <- classes("context", "river")
lake_sty <- reg_main$layers$lake
town_sty <- reg_main$layers$town

# discharge classes: labels that restate the breaks are built from them
mad_breaks <- c(0, 0.1, 0.5, 2, 10, 50, Inf)
mad_width <- c(0.15, 0.25, 0.4, 0.6, 0.85, 1.1)
fmt_q <- function(x) format(x, drop0trailing = TRUE, trim = TRUE)
pal_mad$labels[] <- c(paste("Under", fmt_q(mad_breaks[2])),
                      paste0(fmt_q(mad_breaks[2:5]), "–", fmt_q(mad_breaks[3:6])),
                      paste(fmt_q(mad_breaks[6]), "or more"))
mad_class <- function(q) factor(names(pal_mad$values)[findInterval(q, mad_breaks)], names(pal_mad$values))
# the one error scale: every figure, map and table below uses these classes
err_cut <- 20
pal_err$labels[] <- c(paste0("More than ", err_cut, "% under"), paste0("0–", err_cut, "% under"),
                      paste0("0–", err_cut, "% over"), paste0("More than ", err_cut, "% over"))
# within ±err_cut (the table's test, ends included) is the two middle classes
err_class <- function(e) {
  k <- ifelse(e < -err_cut, 1L, ifelse(e < 0, 2L, ifelse(e <= err_cut, 3L, 4L)))
  factor(names(pal_err$values)[k], names(pal_err$values))
}
err_scale <- function(name = "Error against\nthe gauge") {
  # drop = FALSE keeps a class no gauge falls in; override.aes gives it a symbol
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_err$values, labels = pal_err$labels, name = name, drop = FALSE,
                    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21, size = 2.6, colour = "black")))
}

group_name <- stats::setNames(map$groups$watershed_group_name, map$groups$watershed_group_code)
group_km2 <- stats::setNames(map$groups$area_km2, map$groups$watershed_group_code)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
            theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))
pct <- function(x) paste0(round(x), "%")
pct1 <- function(x) paste0(format(round(x, 1), nsmall = 1), "%")
# signed whole percents, with a zero that rounds from either side printed as 0%
signed <- function(x, d = 0) {
  s <- sub("^[+-](0(\\.0+)?%)$", "\\1", sprintf(paste0("%+.", d, "f%%"), x))
  sub("^-", "−", s)
}
num <- function(x, d = 0) format(round(x, d), big.mark = ",", nsmall = d)
and_text <- function(x) sub(", ([^,]*)$", " and \\1", paste(x, collapse = ", "))
to_title <- function(x) {
  vapply(strsplit(tolower(x), " "), function(w) {
    big <- !w %in% c("at", "the", "near", "of", "in", "above", "below", "north")
    w[big] <- paste0(toupper(substring(w[big], 1, 1)), substring(w[big], 2))
    paste(w, collapse = " ")
  }, "")
}

# every station the text or a table names must sit inside a map's frame; each
# is recorded where it is named, and each map records what its frame holds
named <- character()
drawn <- character()
in_frame <- function(pts, bb) {
  xy <- sf::st_coordinates(pts)
  pts$station_number[xy[, 1] > bb[["xmin"]] & xy[, 1] < bb[["xmax"]] &
                       xy[, 2] > bb[["ymin"]] & xy[, 2] < bb[["ymax"]]]
}
as_pts <- function(x) sf::st_transform(sf::st_as_sf(x, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE), 3005)

sk <- v$skill
```

```{r product}
parts <- pub$parts
ds <- function(x) paste0("discharge/fwa/v1/", x)
seg_parts <- parts[parts$dataset == ds("segment_monthly"), ]
ws_parts <- parts[parts$dataset == ds("watershed_monthly"), ]
reader <- pub$reader
n_pick <- stats::setNames(reader$picked, reader$source)
# the two datasets, and only the balance in the watershed table
stopifnot(nrow(seg_parts) + nrow(ws_parts) == nrow(parts), all(ws_parts$source == "wet_balance"),
          setequal(seg_parts$source, c("pcic_routed", "wet_balance")),
          sum(seg_parts$rows) == sum(reader$rows))
# segments with each source (13 rows each), and with both: "most segments have both"
n_src <- stats::setNames(reader$rows / 13, reader$source)
n_both_src <- sum(n_src) - sum(n_pick)
stopifnot(all(n_src == round(n_src)), n_both_src > 0.5 * sum(n_pick))
built <- as.Date(substr(pub$built, 1, 10))
built_text <- paste(as.integer(format(built, "%d")), format(built, "%B %Y"))
```

wet publishes the mean flow of every stream segment in British Columbia's
Freshwater Atlas, in cubic metres per second, for each calendar month and for
the year, from two sources. It is public at
`s3://fresh-bc/discharge/fwa/v1/`, and its manifest,
<`r pub$manifest`>, lists every part with its rows, size and md5. The bucket
allows no listing, so a reader starts from the manifest. The current build
has `r nrow(parts)` parquet parts, `r format(round(sum(parts$bytes) / 1e9, 2), nsmall = 2)`
GB, built on `r built_text` at wet commit `r pub$wet_commit`.

- **`segment_monthly`**: one row per Freshwater Atlas segment, month and
  source with a value, `r num(sum(seg_parts$rows))` rows. Month 0 is the
  annual mean and months 1–12 the calendar months.
- **`watershed_monthly`**: the same per fundamental watershed, the small
  polygon each segment drains, from the open water balance only
  (`r num(sum(ws_parts$rows))` rows).

Each row comes from one `source`: `pcic_routed`, PCIC's routed flow over
1951–2012, or `wet_balance`, wet's open water balance over 1981–2010, and
`r num(n_both_src)` segments have both. `pick` is TRUE on one of them, the default: routed
PCIC, unless its annual flow is under a fifth of the balance's on a segment
that lies on its own watershed's line, where the balance is picked. Where only
one source has a value, `pick` takes it. Of the
`r num(sum(n_pick))` segments with a value, `r num(n_pick[["pcic_routed"]])`
pick routed PCIC and `r num(n_pick[["wet_balance"]])` the balance.

```{r read, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
library(wet)
cat <- wet_catalog()   # the manifest: one row per part, with its href

# into Postgres (discharge.fwa_v1_segment_monthly), then the default annual flow
conn <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), dbname = "fwapg")
wet_db_load(conn, cat)
DBI::dbGetQuery(conn, "
  select linear_feature_id, q_m3s as mad_m3s
  from discharge.fwa_v1_segment_monthly
  where scenario = 'historical' and month = 0 and pick")

# or straight from the parts: scenario, forcing and source are in the path,
# not the files, so read them with hive_partitioning
duck <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
DBI::dbExecute(duck, "LOAD httpfs")
segs <- cat$href[cat$dataset == "discharge/fwa/v1/segment_monthly"]
DBI::dbGetQuery(duck, sprintf("
  SELECT source, linear_feature_id, q_m3s
  FROM read_parquet([%s], hive_partitioning = true)
  WHERE watershed_group_code = 'SALR' AND month = 0 AND pick",
  paste0("'", segs, "'", collapse = ", ")))
```

Besides flow (`q_m3s`) a row carries `runoff_mm`, the same water as a depth
over the area upstream (NA for a routed row off its watershed's own line,
where the only area is another stream's), `coverage`, the share of that area
the balance's inputs cover, and `period`, the years averaged. Parts are split
by top-level drainage and sorted by `watershed_group_code`, so a read for one
group opens a few row groups.

## How each source was made

**Routed PCIC.** The Pacific Climate Impacts Consortium runs the VIC-GL model
of snow, glaciers, soil and runoff on a 0.0625° grid, driven by the PNWNAmet
observed climate, and routes its runoff down rivers with the Raven model to
outlets of its own network
([hydromosaic](https://beehive.pacificclimate.org/chyp/)). New Graph's
[fork of fwapg](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/fwapg/pull/6) places
those outlets on Freshwater Atlas segments and spreads the flow between
outlets by drainage area, giving each segment monthly means over 1951–2012.
The annual value is the mean of the twelve. It covers the Fraser, Peace,
Columbia and most of the coast, but not the Liard.

**Open water balance.** wet's own estimate, after
[Chapman et al. (2018)](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/assets/gov/environment/air-land-water/water/northeast-water-strategy/chapman_et_al-2018-jawra.pdf).
Precipitation less actual evapotranspiration, from 1981–2010 normals on a 30″
grid, is averaged over each watershed's upstream area, then adjusted per
[hydrologic zone](https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/bc-hydrologic-zones)
against gauges in the Water Survey of Canada's
[HYDAT](https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/services/water-overview/quantity/monitoring/survey/data-products-services/national-archive-hydat.html)
archive. It covers all of BC, and its code and inputs are open. The published
values come from the fit that uses every gauge; the scores below hold each
gauge out of the fit that predicts it.

## How the numbers line up at the gauges

```{r scores}
both <- sk[!is.na(sk$routed_mm), ]
both$rt_err <- 100 * (both$routed_mm / both$obs - 1)
n_both <- nrow(both)
score <- function(e) {
  q <- stats::quantile(e, c(0.25, 0.75))
  c(mae = mean(abs(e)), bias = mean(e), lo = q[[1]], hi = q[[2]], within = 100 * mean(abs(e) <= err_cut))
}
s_rt <- score(both$rt_err)
s_wb <- score(both$err_pct)
s_all <- score(sk$err_pct)
fmt_score <- function(s) {
  c(pct1(s[["mae"]]), signed(s[["bias"]], 1), paste(signed(s[["lo"]]), "to", signed(s[["hi"]])), pct(s[["within"]]))
}
score_tab <- data.frame(
  ` ` = c("Mean absolute error", "Bias (mean error)", "Middle half of errors", sprintf("Within ±%d%%", err_cut)),
  `Routed PCIC` = fmt_score(s_rt),
  `Open water balance (held out)` = fmt_score(s_wb),
  check.names = FALSE
)
names(score_tab)[2:3] <- paste0(names(score_tab)[2:3], ", ", n_both, " gauges")
score_tab[[sprintf("Open water balance (held out), all %d gauges", nrow(sk))]] <- fmt_score(s_all)
# the gauges without routed flow are mostly in the Liard (10x)
none <- sk[is.na(sk$routed_mm), ]
stopifnot(nrow(none) > 0, mean(startsWith(none$station_number, "10")) > 0.5)

mae_of <- function(i) mean(abs(sk$err_pct[i]))
mae_head <- mae_of(sk$nesting == "headwater")
mae_nest <- mae_of(sk$nesting == "nested")
small_km2 <- 100
large_km2 <- 1000
mae_small <- mae_of(sk$area_km2 < small_km2)
mae_large <- mae_of(sk$area_km2 >= large_km2)
zone_mae <- sort(tapply(abs(sk$err_pct), sk$zone, mean))
worst <- names(zone_mae)[length(zone_mae)]
worst_name <- to_title(map$zones$name[map$zones$zone == worst])
n_worst <- sum(sk$zone == worst)
# the prose: nested gauges score better than headwater, small basins worse than
# large, and the worst zone is a semi-arid interior plateau (15, 17, 23 or 24:
# research/water_balance_method.md) that stands out at twice the average
stopifnot(mae_nest < mae_head, mae_small > mae_large, sum(zone_mae > 2 * s_all[["mae"]]) == 1,
          worst %in% c("15", "17", "23", "24"), length(worst_name) == 1)
sk$class <- err_class(sk$err_pct)

err_lim <- c(-100, 200)
n_off <- sum(both$err_pct > err_lim[2] | both$rt_err > err_lim[2])
cap_cmp <- sprintf(paste(
  "Error at each of the %d calibration gauges both sources cover: routed PCIC's across, the water",
  "balance's (held out) up. The shaded square holds the gauges both put within ±%d%%. Between the dashed",
  "diagonals, the left and right wedges hold gauges where the balance is closer, the top and bottom wedges",
  "those where routed PCIC is.%s"
), n_both, err_cut,
if (n_off) sprintf(" %d gauge%s beyond +%d%% %s drawn at the edge.", n_off, if (n_off > 1) "s" else "",
                   err_lim[2], if (n_off > 1) "are" else "is") else "")
cap_prov <- sprintf(paste(
  "The %d calibration gauges, filled by the water balance's held-out error at each. Routed PCIC's",
  "coverage is outlined; zone %s, the weakest, is shaded; the %s, mapped below, is in black."
), nrow(sk), worst, group_name[["SALR"]])
```

Both sources are scored against mean annual runoff measured at the
`r nrow(sk)` HYDAT gauges the water balance is calibrated on, over 1981–2010.
Error is modelled minus observed runoff, as a percentage of observed. The
balance is scored *held out*: wet holds out each Water Survey sub-sub-drainage
in turn (the first four characters of a station number, such as 08EE), fits
on the rest and predicts the gauges it held out, so a gauge's neighbours on
the same river cannot vouch for it. Routed PCIC has a value at
`r n_both` of the gauges; most of the other `r nrow(none)` are in the Liard.

```{r score-table}
knitr::kable(score_tab, align = "lrrr", row.names = FALSE,
             caption = paste(
               "Error in mean annual runoff at the calibration gauges. PCIC does not list the gauges it",
               "calibrated to, so its errors may be partly in sample, and its flow covers 1951–2012",
               "against observations over 1981–2010."
             ))
```

```{r compare, fig.width = 5.5, fig.height = 5.5, out.width = "80%", fig.cap = cap_cmp}
sq <- data.frame(xmin = -err_cut, xmax = err_cut, ymin = -err_cut, ymax = err_cut)
both_plot <- both
both_plot$rt_err <- pmin(both_plot$rt_err, err_lim[2])
both_plot$err_pct <- pmin(both_plot$err_pct, err_lim[2])
ggplot(both_plot, aes(rt_err, err_pct)) +
  geom_rect(data = sq, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            fill = pal_prov$values[["zone"]], alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = pal_guide$values[["one_to_one"]],
              linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_abline(slope = -1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = pal_guide$values[["one_to_one"]],
              linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = nesting), size = 1.6, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_skill$values[c("headwater", "nested")],
                      labels = pal_skill$labels[c("headwater", "nested")], name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = err_lim, labels = function(x) sub("^\\+0%$", "0%", signed(x))) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = err_lim, labels = function(x) sub("^\\+0%$", "0%", signed(x))) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.75 * err_lim[2], y = 0.1 * err_lim[2], label = "balance closer", size = 3,
           colour = pal_guide$values[["one_to_one"]]) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.1 * err_lim[2], y = 0.9 * err_lim[2], label = "routed closer", size = 3,
           colour = pal_guide$values[["one_to_one"]]) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = "Routed PCIC error", y = "Water balance error (held out)")
```

A nested gauge's basin holds another gauge's; a headwater gauge's does not.
Held out, the balance averages `r pct(mae_nest)` error at nested gauges and
`r pct(mae_head)` at headwater ones, and `r pct(mae_large)` on basins over
`r num(large_km2)` km² against `r pct(mae_small)` on those under
`r small_km2` km². One of BC's `r nrow(map$zones)` hydrologic zones stands
out: zone `r worst`, the `r worst_name`, a semi-arid interior plateau, where
its `r n_worst` gauges average `r pct(zone_mae[[worst]])`.

```{r map-province, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6.6, fig.cap = cap_prov}
gpts <- as_pts(sk)
zone_w <- map$zones[map$zones$zone == worst, ]
bb_bc <- gq::gq_bbox_aspect(sf::st_bbox(bc), asp = 7 / 5.6)
lab_g <- sf::st_centroid(map$groups)
lab_g$label <- group_name[lab_g$watershed_group_code]
xy_g <- sf::st_coordinates(lab_g)
dx_bc <- bb_bc[["xmax"]] - bb_bc[["xmin"]]
dy_bc <- bb_bc[["ymax"]] - bb_bc[["ymin"]]
sb_km <- max(gq::gq_scale_breaks(bb_bc))
sb <- data.frame(x = bb_bc[["xmin"]] + 0.05 * dx_bc, y = bb_bc[["ymin"]] + 0.05 * dy_bc)
sb$xend <- sb$x + sb_km * 1000
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = bc, fill = "white", colour = pal_map$values[["outline"]], linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_sf(data = zone_w, aes(alpha = "zone"), fill = pal_prov$values[["zone"]], colour = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = map$coverage, aes(linetype = "coverage"), fill = NA, colour = pal_prov$values[["coverage"]],
          linewidth = 0.45) +
  geom_sf(data = map$groups, fill = NA, colour = pal_prov$values[["group"]], linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_label(data = data.frame(x = xy_g[, 1] + 0.03 * dx_bc, y = xy_g[, 2], label = lab_g$label),
             aes(x, y, label = label), hjust = 0, size = 2.8, linewidth = 0, fill = "white", alpha = 0.6,
             label.padding = unit(1.2, "pt")) +
  geom_sf(data = gpts, aes(fill = class), shape = 21, colour = "black", size = 1.7, stroke = 0.25) +
  geom_segment(data = sb, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = y), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(data = sb, aes(x = (x + xend) / 2, y = y, label = paste(sb_km, "km")), vjust = -0.7, size = 3) +
  err_scale("Held-out error") +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(zone = 1), labels = sprintf("Zone %s, %s", worst, worst_name), name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(coverage = "dashed"), labels = pal_prov$labels[["coverage"]], name = NULL) +
  coord_sf(xlim = bb_bc[c("xmin", "xmax")], ylim = bb_bc[c("ymin", "ymax")], expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1, ncol = 2), alpha = guide_legend(order = 2),
         linetype = guide_legend(order = 3)) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical", legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
        panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = pal_map$values[["outline"]], linewidth = 0.3))
```

## Salmon River: both sources side by side

```{r map-data}
seg <- merge(map$segments, v$segments, by = c("linear_feature_id", "watershed_group_code"))
stopifnot(nrow(seg) == nrow(map$segments))
n_no_value <- sum(is.na(seg$mad_wb_m3s))
# the limits bullet: neither source has these, and there are some
stopifnot(n_no_value > 0, all(is.na(seg$mad_routed_m3s[is.na(seg$mad_wb_m3s)])))
order_no_value <- range(seg$stream_order[is.na(seg$mad_wb_m3s)])
no_value_text <- if (n_no_value == 1) {
  sprintf("one segment of order %d or more has none, of order %d", prov$min_order, order_no_value[1])
} else {
  sprintf("%d segments of order %d or more have none, of order %d to %d", n_no_value, prov$min_order,
          order_no_value[1], order_no_value[2])
}
n_total <- nrow(seg)
seg <- seg[!is.na(seg$mad_wb_m3s), ]
salr_pick <- table(factor(seg$pick, c("pcic_routed", "wet_balance")))
stopifnot(sum(salr_pick) == nrow(seg))
pick_text <- if (salr_pick[["wet_balance"]] == 0) {
  sprintf("all %s of its segments with a value", num(nrow(seg)))
} else {
  sprintf("%s of its %s segments with a value, and the balance on %s", num(salr_pick[["pcic_routed"]]),
          num(nrow(seg)), num(salr_pick[["wet_balance"]]))
}

# the scale bar's place, and the box it and its text take, which labels avoid
scale_bar_at <- function(bb) {
  dx <- bb[["xmax"]] - bb[["xmin"]]
  dy <- bb[["ymax"]] - bb[["ymin"]]
  km <- max(gq::gq_scale_breaks(bb))
  sb <- data.frame(x = bb[["xmin"]] + 0.05 * dx, y = bb[["ymin"]] + 0.04 * dy, km = km)
  sb$xend <- sb$x + km * 1000
  sb$x0 <- sb$x
  sb$x1 <- sb$xend
  sb$y0 <- sb$y - 0.01 * dy
  sb$y1 <- sb$y + 0.06 * dy
  sb
}
mad_scales <- list(
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_mad$values, labels = pal_mad$labels, name = "Mean annual\ndischarge (m³/s)",
                      drop = FALSE),
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = stats::setNames(mad_width, names(pal_mad$values)), labels = pal_mad$labels,
                         name = "Mean annual\ndischarge (m³/s)", drop = FALSE)
)
# labels for towns and gauges, placed greedily: gauges first, each beside its
# point (right, left, above, below) where it overlaps no point, no label placed
# before it and no frame edge; failing that, where it overlaps least. Box sizes
# are estimated from the text size and the panel's size in inches
map_labels <- function(towns, gauges, bb, width_in, height_in, avoid = NULL) {
  in_bb <- function(xy) {
    xy[, 1] > bb[["xmin"]] & xy[, 1] < bb[["xmax"]] & xy[, 2] > bb[["ymin"]] & xy[, 2] < bb[["ymax"]]
  }
  tx <- sf::st_coordinates(towns)
  towns <- towns[in_bb(tx), ]
  tx <- tx[in_bb(tx), , drop = FALSE]
  gx <- sf::st_coordinates(gauges)
  ux <- (bb[["xmax"]] - bb[["xmin"]]) / width_in    # map units per inch
  uy <- (bb[["ymax"]] - bb[["ymin"]]) / height_in
  item <- data.frame(x = c(gx[, 1], tx[, 1]), y = c(gx[, 2], tx[, 2]),
                     label = c(gauges$station_number, towns$name),
                     size = rep(c(2.6, 2.8), c(nrow(gx), nrow(tx))),
                     town = rep(c(FALSE, TRUE), c(nrow(gx), nrow(tx))))
  pt <- item$size * 72.27 / 25.4
  item$w <- nchar(item$label) * pt * ifelse(item$town, 0.66, 0.6) / 72 * ux
  item$h <- pt * 1.5 / 72 * uy
  r <- 0.06 * ux   # half a symbol, as an obstacle
  boxes <- data.frame(x0 = item$x - r, x1 = item$x + r, y0 = item$y - r, y1 = item$y + r)
  if (!is.null(avoid)) boxes <- rbind(boxes, avoid[c("x0", "x1", "y0", "y1")])
  overlap <- function(b, others) {
    ox <- pmax(0, pmin(b$x1, others$x1) - pmax(b$x0, others$x0))
    oy <- pmax(0, pmin(b$y1, others$y1) - pmax(b$y0, others$y0))
    sum(ox * oy)
  }
  gap <- 0.07 * ux
  out <- vector("list", nrow(item))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(item))) {
    w <- item$w[i]
    h <- item$h[i]
    x <- item$x[i]
    y <- item$y[i]
    cand <- data.frame(hjust = c(0, 1, 0.5, 0.5), vjust = c(0.5, 0.5, 0, 1),
                       lx = c(x + gap, x - gap, x, x), ly = c(y, y, y + gap, y - gap))
    cand$x0 <- cand$lx - cand$hjust * w
    cand$x1 <- cand$x0 + w
    cand$y0 <- cand$ly - cand$vjust * h
    cand$y1 <- cand$y0 + h
    cost <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(cand)), function(k) {
      b <- cand[k, ]
      edge <- (b$x0 < bb[["xmin"]]) + (b$x1 > bb[["xmax"]]) + (b$y0 < bb[["ymin"]]) + (b$y1 > bb[["ymax"]])
      overlap(b, boxes[-i, ]) + edge * w * h
    }, 0)
    k <- which.min(cost)
    out[[i]] <- cand[k, c("lx", "ly", "hjust", "vjust")]
    boxes <- rbind(boxes, cand[k, c("x0", "x1", "y0", "y1")])
  }
  lab <- cbind(item[c("label", "town")], do.call(rbind, out))
  list(geom_point(data = data.frame(x = tx[, 1], y = tx[, 2]), aes(x, y), size = 1.1,
                  colour = town_sty$label$color),
       geom_label(data = lab[lab$town, ], aes(lx, ly, label = label, hjust = hjust, vjust = vjust),
                  colour = town_sty$label$color, fontface = "bold", size = 2.8, linewidth = 0, fill = "white",
                  alpha = 0.8, label.padding = unit(1.2, "pt")),
       geom_label(data = lab[!lab$town, ], aes(lx, ly, label = label, hjust = hjust, vjust = vjust),
                  size = 2.6, linewidth = 0, fill = "white", alpha = 0.85, label.padding = unit(1, "pt")))
}

# both sources, and the gauges that arbitrate between them
ratio_salr <- stats::median(seg$mad_wb_m3s / seg$mad_routed_m3s, na.rm = TRUE)
ga <- v$gauges_salr
ga$wb_err <- 100 * (ga$wb_mm / ga$obs_mm - 1)
ga$rt_err <- 100 * (ga$routed_mm / ga$obs_mm - 1)
outlet <- ga[ga$holds_salr, ]
ga$rt_closer <- abs(ga$rt_err) < abs(ga$wb_err)   # a column, so it follows the reorder below
# the prose: the balance reads high at every gauge; routed PCIC is closer at
# most of them, the outlet among them, and the balance at the rest, where
# routed PCIC is off by more than it is
stopifnot(ratio_salr > 1, all(ga$wb_err > 0), nrow(outlet) == 1,
          sum(ga$rt_closer) > nrow(ga) / 2, any(!ga$rt_closer), ga$rt_closer[ga$holds_salr],
          all(abs(ga$rt_err[!ga$rt_closer]) > 10))
ga <- ga[order(!ga$holds_salr, ga$area_km2), ]
named <- c(named, ga$station_number)
gauge_tab <- data.frame(
  Gauge = sprintf("%s %s", ga$station_number, to_title(ga$station_name)),
  `Area (km²)` = num(ga$area_km2),
  `Observed (mm)` = num(ga$obs_mm),
  `Water balance (held out)` = signed(ga$wb_err),
  `Routed PCIC` = signed(ga$rt_err),
  check.names = FALSE
)

# the Salmon River frame: the group, every gauge in the table and every town a
# gauge is named for ("near Prince George"), inside the context box the map
# layers were cut to
salr <- map$groups
ga_pts <- as_pts(ga)
salr_w <- 3.4
salr_h <- 4.4
pl_near <- map$places[vapply(toupper(map$places$name),
                             function(n) any(grepl(n, ga$station_name, fixed = TRUE)), NA), ]
stopifnot(nrow(pl_near) > 0)
bb_salr <- sf::st_bbox(sf::st_buffer(sf::st_union(c(sf::st_geometry(salr), sf::st_geometry(ga_pts),
                                                    sf::st_geometry(pl_near))), 8000))
bb_salr <- gq::gq_bbox_aspect(bb_salr, asp = salr_w / salr_h)
ctx <- sf::st_bbox(map$context)
stopifnot(bb_salr[["xmin"]] >= ctx[["xmin"]], bb_salr[["xmax"]] <= ctx[["xmax"]],
          bb_salr[["ymin"]] >= ctx[["ymin"]], bb_salr[["ymax"]] <= ctx[["ymax"]])
drawn <- c(drawn, in_frame(ga_pts, bb_salr))
sb_salr <- scale_bar_at(bb_salr)   # bottom left: Prince George sits bottom right

products <- c(routed = "Routed PCIC", wb = "Open water balance")
s2 <- rbind(transform(seg, product = products[["routed"]], class = mad_class(seg$mad_routed_m3s)),
            transform(seg, product = products[["wb"]], class = mad_class(seg$mad_wb_m3s)))
s2$product <- factor(s2$product, products)
s2 <- s2[order(s2$class), ]   # large rivers drawn last, on top
g2 <- rbind(transform(ga_pts, product = products[["routed"]], class = err_class(ga_pts$rt_err)),
            transform(ga_pts, product = products[["wb"]], class = err_class(ga_pts$wb_err)))
g2$product <- factor(g2$product, products)
lakes_salr <- rbind(map$lakes[c("gnis_name", "area_ha")], map$context_lakes[c("gnis_name", "area_ha")])
cap_salr <- sprintf(paste(
  "Published mean annual discharge on %s of the %s %s segments of order %d or more, from routed PCIC",
  "(left) and the open water balance (right), with the gauges of the table filled by each source's",
  "error. Rivers outside the group are grey."
), num(nrow(seg)), num(n_total), group_name[["SALR"]], prov$min_order)
```

The `r group_name[["SALR"]]` is a headwater group of the Fraser
(`r num(group_km2[["SALR"]])` km²). Both sources cover it, and they differ:
the balance gives a median `r format(round(ratio_salr, 2), nsmall = 2)` times
routed PCIC's flow per segment. `pick` takes routed PCIC on
`r pick_text`. The
`r nrow(ga)` gauges in and around the group show how each compares with
measured flow.

The balance runs high at all of them, by `r signed(min(ga$wb_err))` to
`r signed(max(ga$wb_err))`. Routed PCIC is closer at `r sum(ga$rt_closer)`,
including `r outlet$station_number`, the gauge that drains the whole group:
`r signed(outlet$rt_err)` against the balance's `r signed(outlet$wb_err)`. The
balance is closer at the other `r sum(!ga$rt_closer)`, where routed PCIC is off
by `r and_text(signed(ga$rt_err[!ga$rt_closer]))`.

```{r gauges-salr}
knitr::kable(gauge_tab, align = "lrrrr", row.names = FALSE,
             caption = sprintf(paste(
               "Calibration gauges within %d km of the %s group, and its outlet gauge (first row):",
               "mean annual runoff observed in 1981–2010, and each source's error against it."
             ), prov$near_km, group_name[["SALR"]]))
```

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = salr, fill = pal_map$values[["group"]], colour = pal_map$values[["outline"]], linewidth = 0.4) +

## Limits

```{r limits}
# the bullet: the adjustment ships although the headwater gate does not pass
# (a recorded override, #43), and pooled zones get none
stopifnot(isTRUE(prov$keep_adjust), isFALSE(prov$gate_pass), identical(prov$pooled_variant, "none"))
```

- **Coverage.** Routed PCIC has no value, or almost none, in the Liard and in
  a few northern and border basins (the Yukon and Alsek headwaters, the Hay,
  the Skagit), and on the outer coast's islands it reaches only some segments.
  There `pick` takes the balance.
- **Dry zones.** In zone `r worst` and the other semi-arid interior zones,
  runoff is a small remainder of precipitation, so a small error in
  evapotranspiration is a large one in runoff.
- **The zone adjustment is a close call on headwater basins.** On headwater
  gauges it does not beat raw precipitation less evapotranspiration, and it is
  kept by a recorded decision for what it does on larger rivers
  (`research/water_balance_method.md`, "Refit on HYDAT 2026-07-17"). Zones
  with too few gauges for their own adjustment get none.
- **Small streams.** `r sum(sk$area_km2 < small_km2)` of the `r nrow(sk)`
  gauges drain less than `r small_km2` km², and there the balance averages
  `r pct(mae_small)` held-out error.
- **Segments without a watershed.** A segment with no watershed polygon in
  the Freshwater Atlas lookup gets a value from neither source. In the
  `r group_name[["SALR"]]`, `r no_value_text`, left off the map.

## Validation

Every published value is checked against what it was built from when the
product is built: routed months against fwapg's table, routed annual values
against their twelve months, the balance against the fit's output, and every
row against the per-segment table it was cut from. The counts compared and
differing are in the build report,
[`r basename(pub$report)`](`r paste0("https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/wet/blob/main/", pub$report)`).
This article reads its segment values from the published parts and is not
built unless each equals its source. wet's own path through PCIC's gridded
output reproduces fwapg's earlier unrouted annual table on the Salmon River to
the five decimals fwapg stores, and the effect of sampling grid cells by area
rather than at each watershed's centroid is measured there too
([research](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/wet/blob/main/research/fwapg_mad_method.md)).

```{r provenance}
chk <- prov$published_check
```

**Cached inputs.** This article runs on saved outputs. Segment values were
read on `r paste(as.integer(format(prov$built, "%d")), format(prov$built, "%B %Y"))`
from the published build `r pub$wet_commit` (segment table
`r pub$segment_commit`), `r num(sum(chk$compared))` of them checked against
their sources with none differing, by `data-raw/segment_vignette_data.R` at
wet commit `r prov$wet_commit`. Gauge scores are from province run
`r prov$province_run` (annual AET `r prov$aet`, HYDAT release
`r substr(prov$hydat_release, 1, 10)`), and routed PCIC from fwapg at commit
`r prov$routed_commit` (`r prov$routed_fingerprint`), scored in
`r prov$routed_report`. Map layers come from the Freshwater Atlas (fwapg), BC
Geographic Names and the BC Hydrologic Zones, by
`data-raw/segment_vignette_map.R`.

```{r named-on-map}
# every station named in the prose or a table is inside a map's frame: the
# tables add theirs above, and any station number typed into the prose is added here
f <- knitr::current_input()
if (!is.null(f)) {
  x <- readLines(f, warn = FALSE)
  named <- c(named, unlist(regmatches(x, gregexpr("\\b0[0-9][A-Z]{2}[0-9]{3}\\b", x))))
}
named <- unique(c(named, outlet$station_number))
missing <- setdiff(named, drawn)
if (length(missing)) stop("named but not on a map: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
```

```{r wordcount, include = FALSE}
if (!is.null(f)) {
  y <- utils::tail(x, -utils::head(which(x == "---"), 2)[2])   # drop the YAML header
  fence <- cumsum(grepl("^```", y)) %% 2 == 1
  y <- y[!fence & !grepl("^```", y)]
  y <- gsub("`r [^`]*`", "", y)          # inline code is not body prose
  y <- y[!grepl("^\\s*$", y)]
  n <- sum(lengths(strsplit(trimws(y), "\\s+")))
  message("body prose: ", n, " words")
  cap <- 1200
  if (n > cap) stop("body prose is ", n, " words; the cap is ", cap)
}
```
